To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the DNA fingerprint of chorionic villi is identical to that of the embryo and that the DNA fingerprint pattern of the decidual membrane represents the mother’s.
the chorion villi of a placenta are genetically identical to the embryo and the DNA fingerprinting of the chorion villis can be used for paternity testing during the first trimesters of a pregnancy.
the chorionic villi of a fetus contain the same DNA fingerprint as the fetus, while the DNA fingerprint of the decidua membrane is that of the mother.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the analysis of genomic DNA polymorphisms detected in the human genome by a minisatteelite called tentatively “MyO” which corresponds to the minisatteelite in the human myoglobin gene (Jeffreys et al. 1985a).
the analysis of the DNA fingerprint of the human placenta, especially the chorionic villus.
the application of DNA fingerprinting to forensic medicine, especially for paternity determination during early pregnancy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the DNA fingerprints from chorionic villus are essential for paternity determination in the first trimester, which can be achieved by chorionic villus biopsy.
the chorion villi represent the embryonal tissue and the decidual tissue represents the maternal tissue in the placenta.

the analysis of DNA fingerprint of the chorion villi, which can be obtained by chorionic villus biopsy, would be a reliable method for the determination of paternity during the first trimesters of a pregnancy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
it is possible to determine the paternity by the chorionic villus biopsy, which is performed during the first trimesters of a pregnancy.
a DNA fingerprinting analysis from a chorionic villus biopsy sample is a reliable and effective method for a prenatal paternity determination.
the DNA fingerprinting is a powerful tool for the forensic medicine, which is applicable to the early prenatal diagnosis.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the DNA fingerprint pattern of the chorion villi is a good indicator of the fetal DNA fingerprint, and that the DNA fingerprint of the decidual tissue is a good indicator for the maternal DNA fingerprint.
we should not be too quick to assume that the presence of a particular gene or protein in a particular tissue is due to its function in that tissue.
the DNA fingerprint of the chorionic villus represents the essential embryonic DNA fingerprint pattern, and that it can provide the possibility to determine the paternity in the first trimester.
